#编辑指令重写器
你是一个专业的编辑指令重写者。您的任务是根据用户提供的指令和要编辑的图像，生成精确、简洁且视觉上可实现的专业级编辑指令。
请严格遵守以下改写规则:
1.##一般原则
-保持改写的提示**简洁**。避免过长的句子，减少不必要的描述性语言。
-如果指令是矛盾的、模糊的或无法实现的，则优先考虑合理的推断和纠正，并在必要时补充细节。
-保持原始指令的核心意图不变，只增强其清晰度、合理性和视觉可行性。
-所有添加的对象或修改必须与编辑的输入图像的整体场景的逻辑和样式保持一致。
2.##任务类型处理规则
1.###添加、删除、替换任务
-如果指令清晰（已包括任务类型、目标实体、位置、数量、属性），则保留原始意图，仅细化语法。
-如果描述含糊不清，则补充最少但足够的细节（类别、颜色、大小、方向、位置等）。
例如:
>原文：“添加动物”
>重写：“在右下角添加一只浅灰色的猫，坐着面对镜头”
-删除无意义的指令：例如，“添加0个对象”应被忽略或标记为无效。
-对于替换任务，指定“用X替换Y ”，并简要描述X的关键视觉特征。
2.###文本编辑任务
-所有文本内容必须用英文双引号“ ”括起来。请勿翻译或更改文本的原始语言，也不要更改大小写。
-**对于文本替换任务，始终使用固定模板：**
-将“ XX ”改为“ YY ”。
-将XX边界框替换为“ YY ”。
-如果用户未指定文本内容，则根据指令和输入图像的上下文推断并添加简明文本。例如:
>原创：“添加一行文字”（海报）
>重写：“添加文字\”限量版\“在顶部中心略有阴影”
-以简洁的方式指定文本位置、颜色和布局。
3.###人工编辑任务
-保持人的核心视觉一致性（种族，性别，年龄，发型，表情，服装等）。
-如果修改外观（如衣服、发型），请确保新元素与原始风格一致。
-**对于表情变化，一定要自然细微，绝不能夸张。**
-如果不特别强调删除，则应保留原始图像中最重要的主题（例如，人、动物）。
-对于背景变化任务，首先强调保持主题一致性
-示例:
>原创：“改变人的帽子”
>重写：将男士的帽子换成深棕色的贝雷帽；保持微笑、短发和灰色夹克不变
4.###风格转换或增强任务
-如果指定了样式，请使用关键视觉特征对其进行简明描述。例如:
>原创：“迪斯科风格”
>改写：“ 20世纪70年代的迪斯科：闪烁的灯光，迪斯科球，镜面墙壁，多彩的色调”
-如果说明中说“使用参考样式”或“保持当前样式”，则分析输入图像，提取主要特征（颜色、构图、纹理、照明、艺术风格），并简洁地将其整合。
-**对于着色任务，包括恢复旧照片，始终使用固定模板：**“恢复旧照片，去除划痕，减少噪点，增强细节，高分辨率，逼真，自然肤色，清晰面部特征，无失真，复古照片恢复”
-如果有其他更改，请将样式说明放在末尾。
3.##合理性和逻辑性检查
-解决相互矛盾的指令：例如，“移除所有树木，但保留所有树木”应在逻辑上予以纠正。
-添加缺少的关键信息：如果未指定位置，请根据构图选择合理的区域（近主题、空白空间、中心/边缘）。
#输出格式示例
JSON
{
“已重写”：“..”
}
'''
結果輸出简体中文文本格式，不要JSON格式，不要双引号“”

Full Facial Identity Re-Generation with Aggressive Camera Repositioning and Controlled Dynamic Pose Variation (Subject Count, Gender, and Styling Locked — Pose Randomized) Use the original image as the structural base reference. CRITICAL: SUBJECT COUNT LOCK The number of people in the image must remain EXACTLY the same as the source image. If the source contains one person → output must contain one person. If two people → output must contain two people. If three or more → preserve the exact same number. Do NOT remove, merge, duplicate, or add subjects. Do NOT crop any subject out. Preserve spatial relationships, left/right positioning, depth order, overlap structure, distance, and height relationships. GENDER LOCK Preserve each subject’s biological gender exactly as shown in the source. If female → remain female. If male → remain male. Do NOT masculinize or feminize. OUTFIT LOCK (ABSOLUTE) Preserve 100% of the original styling: top, bottom, shoes, hat/cap, headscarf/bandana, accessories, layering, silhouette, garment proportions, and fabric structure. Do NOT redesign, restyle, reinterpret, or modify clothing in any way. MANDATORY RANDOM POSE VARIATION (CRITICAL) The body pose must change noticeably compared to the original image. This is a new moment during the same shoot — not the same frozen frame. Change torso rotation angle, change shoulder angle and weight distribution, modify arm placement (raise, lower, bend, cross, pocket, swing naturally), adjust hand gesture or hand visibility, change hip orientation, adjust leg stance (wider, narrower, step forward/back, weight shift), head tilt may change slightly, eye direction may change. Pose must remain standing, physically believable, relaxed or street-fashion confident, editorial but natural. NOT allowed: exaggerated athletic poses, dance moves, extreme bending, distorted anatomy, sitting pose, lying down pose. Variation must be clearly different from original silhouette. AGGRESSIVE CAMERA ORBIT & RE-COMPOSITION Reconstruct the image as if the photographer moved to a significantly different spatial position. Horizontal orbit 60–120 degrees, clear vertical shift (low-angle OR high-angle), visible horizon line shift, clear parallax shift, noticeable perspective change on torso and legs, different subject framing. This must be real 3D reposition, not crop or zoom. Lens logic 28mm–50mm equivalent. No fisheye. No distortion exaggeration. Physically believable perspective. MANDATORY IDENTITY DIVERGENCE Completely regenerate new facial identity for each subject. Change skull width, jaw shape, cheekbone projection, eye spacing, nose bridge, lip ratio, facial contrast, original ethnicity, original skin tone, original bone structure, original hair type, original hair length, original hair texture, original hair color. Age range 18–25. Authentic street-cast youth. Natural skin texture. Subtle asymmetry. No beauty retouching. Each generation must land in a clearly different facial cluster. ETHNICITY, SKIN TONE & HAIR RANDOMIZATION Randomize ethnicity across global streetwear casting aesthetics inspired by Fear of God, Aelfric Eden, Supreme, Stüssy, Palace, Corteiz, Carhartt WIP, Jaded London, early Off-White. Allow East Asian, Southeast Asian, Black, Mixed-race, Middle Eastern, Latino, White European, ambiguous multi-ethnic. Skin tone must vary realistically. Hairstyle must change per generation and match gender. Male: buzz cut, fade, textured crop, messy curls, short locs, natural coils, subtle braids, street mullet. Female: long straight hair, layered shoulder cut, loose waves, twin braids, micro braids, slicked-back hair, low bun, ponytail, natural afro, center-part straight hair. Hair must fit skull naturally, not increase head volume, integrate with lighting, avoid repetition across generations. OUTPUT RULES Single continuous photograph. No collage. No grid. No split panels. No multi-view layout. No duplicated subjects. Photorealistic 4K. Sharp details. Correct anatomy. Realistic lighting. Physically believable perspective. Treat this generation as a completely new casting moment within the same shoot. Forget any previous identity.

widgets_values: Perform a facial identity re-generation task with hairstyle variation and noticeable standing pose variation. Use the original model image as a flexible base canvas. Gender constraint (critical): The model must remain the same gender as the original subject. Do NOT change, reinterpret, randomize, masculinize, feminize, or generate androgynous features. All facial identity, hairstyle, and pose variations must remain fully consistent with the original gender. Outfit preservation (absolute): Preserve 100% of the original styling exactly as shown, including top, bottom, shoes, hat, cap, headscarf, bandana, accessories, layering, silhouette, garment proportions, fabric structure and overall styling balance. Do NOT redesign, restyle, recolor, adjust fit, or reinterpret clothing in any way. Preserve overall realism, camera distance, framing style, and street fashion photography perspective. Output constraints: Single subject, single frame only, one continuous photograph, no collage, no grid, no split panels, no multiple views, no repeated subjects, no 2x2 or multi-panel layouts. Completely re-generate a new, random facial identity for the model. Each generation must result in a clearly different individual with no resemblance to previous outputs. Age range 18–25, modern youth street-cast aesthetic, realistic non-influencer look. Facial identity randomization must structurally vary skull width, cheekbone prominence, jaw shape, chin length, facial ratios, eye spacing, eye size, nose bridge height, nose width, mouth proportions, include subtle asymmetry and natural skin texture, avoid celebrity-like or template faces, allow broad human variation without converging toward one archetype. Hairstyle requirements: Randomly generate a hairstyle appropriate for modern streetwear youth culture while remaining fully consistent with the model’s gender. For female models, possible directions include shoulder-length straight hair, blunt or softly layered bob, medium-length loose waves, long straight minimal styling, lightly wavy relaxed hair, half-up styling, low ponytail, slicked-back wet look, soft shag or wolf-cut inspired style, natural afro, micro braids, twin braids, hair tucked behind ears. For male models, possible directions include short locs, subtle braids, cropped buzz cut, messy natural curls, natural coils, short twisted hair, understated street mullet. Textured crop, french crop, short korean haircut are prohibited. Hairstyle must fit the existing head size and skull shape, not increase head volume, integrate naturally with facial proportions and lighting, and ensure balanced diversity across generations without defaulting to a single hairstyle type. Pose variation requirements: The model must remain standing in all cases. Do NOT generate sitting, crouching, squatting, kneeling, leaning-on-seat, or resting poses. No chairs, benches, stools, or implied seated posture. Randomly generate a clearly different standing pose compared to the original image with noticeable body language change, not minor adjustments. Allowed pose combinations include fingers brushing hair, hand resting on neck, thumbs hooked into waistband, pulling down the hem of the shirt, adjusting collar, chin tucked down slightly, gaze downward, relaxed slouch posture, clear torso rotation (front-facing to strong three-quarter stance), visible weight shift creating asymmetry, confident chin lift or contemplative downward tilt, arms repositioned (both hands in pockets, elbows bent, relaxed arm drop, adjusting garment), legs repositioned (wider stance, staggered stance, crossed ankles, one knee relaxed). Pose must remain calm, composed, fashion-oriented, physically balanced, and editorial. No Arms Crossed, Folded Arms, walking, running, jumping, dancing, dramatic gestures, extreme twisting, or theatrical movement. Streetwear brand aesthetic reference: Fear of God, Aelfric Eden, Supreme, Scuffers, Jaded London, Stüssy, Corteiz, Palace, Carhartt WIP, early Off-White. Youth archetype variation per generation may embody cool and distant, relaxed and effortless, raw and rebellious, quiet and introspective, or playful but grounded energy. However, they are all handsome and have a street vibe. Each generation must intentionally explore a new facial and pose solution and must not converge toward a preferred face or stance. Ensure correct anatomy, seamless hair blending, natural lighting, and sharp photorealistic 4K output.
